_directive: R1 QUESTIONER output for the machines (knit_machine_strategist) self-improvement loop, segment T12, ROUND 2. Adversary who wants the specialist to fail. 8-12 hardest questions the specialist CLAIMS (via competency_questions, owns[], decision_procedure, conflicts_and_dominance) to answer but is most likely to answer weakly, staleley, inconsistently, or by over-claiming. Round 2 targets the SURVIVING weak spots flagged in round1_judgment.json (the two unresolved 'propose' items Q6 used-Stoll toolchain-lock and Q7 non-operational periphery-vs-core test) PLUS fresh un-probed load-bearing joints; it does NOT repeat questions round 1 resolved (Q2 8447-not-6110 duty = OK, Q4 breakeven-undecidable = OK/honesty-exemplary). Each question names the specific failure mode it probes. Questions are NOT answered here. Honesty binding: a gap is a FINDING not something to invent; the three governing blockers (Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece rate, live blended CAC, forward India duty) stay [UNKNOWN]; off-paper = structural mechanism never a named-party accusation; cotton sweater garment duty ~16.5% (6110) never ~7% and never conflated with the 8447 machine-import stack.
round2_targeting_note: Round 1 (dry=false, 6 med findings, 0 high) left two findings UNRESOLVED as 'propose' because they need synthesis/judgment not a mechanical relabel: Q6 (the used-Stoll toolchain-continuity-vs-price rule is not stated as a resolved dominance rule) and Q7 (the periphery-vs-core reverse-engineering rule is a slogan-plus-two-lists with no adjudication test for borderline parts). Round 2 re-attacks BOTH at their hardest edge (Q2-R2, Q3-R2 below) and opens fresh un-probed joints the round-1 set never touched: whether a cheap Cixing-class used machine can even hit the 12GG fine gauge the warm-California product requires (the buy-used default's silent product-fit hole); the whole-garment used band (~$20k-90k) BREACHING the 'sub-$20k used' anchor that the build-NEVER order-of-magnitude comparison rests on; the linker LABOUR-SUPPLY dependency (T1's hardest-to-re-hire role) that the own-a-line and subcontract postures both quietly assume away; the circular logic of the programmer being simultaneously 'the scarcest binding constraint' AND 'the thing AI most offsets'; the whole-garment [UNKNOWN] micro-economics functioning as a self-serving escape hatch; and whether the apply_now relabels round 1 proposed actually neutralize the overclaims or merely re-word them.

questions.q: Your buy-used default is 'Chinese Cixing-class first' at ~$4,000-15,000, yet your own product tier is 12GG fine gauge for warm-California 'elevated basics' and USED_MACHINE_DILIGENCE lists 'gauge' as a condition to check. Can a used machine in that cheap Cixing-class band actually knit at the fine gauge (and hold the fine-count yarn, needle condition, and stitch quality) your own product requires — and if you cannot confirm it does, is your headline first-buy recommendation resting on a machine that may be the wrong gauge for your own sweater?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[4] (buy-used Chinese-Cixing-class-first dominates new); capabilities[0] gauge-to-product fit (12GG for warm California); capabilities[2]/glossary 'buy-used threshold' + 'Cixing-class used machine'; kb2 USED_MACHINE_DILIGENCE ('gauge' check)
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap / unexamined product-fit hole: the buy-used default (a load-bearing owned verdict) is stated at a price tier without ever confirming the machine at that tier can hit the fine gauge the specialist's OWN product needs, so the default may silently recommend a gauge-mismatched machine.
questions.why_load_bearing: the Cixing-class-first buy is the specialist's single most concrete acquisition instruction; if the cheap tier cannot make the 12GG product, the whole 'subcontract->buy-used' ladder's first owned step is either mis-priced (needs a pricier fine-gauge machine) or mis-specified, and the capex the downstream cost model inherits is wrong.

questions.q: Round 1 flagged (Q6, left as 'propose') that the 2025 Stoll exit simultaneously DEEPENS the cheap used pool (a reason to buy used) and LOCKS your scarcest resource — the vendor-locked programmer — into a discontinued, Obertshausen-only toolchain (a reason NOT to buy a used Stoll for the founding machine), and that no single rule resolves this. State the resolved dominance rule: when a bargain used ex-Stoll machine is on the table, does toolchain continuity for the programmer hinge dominate the price bargain or not — and does your spec as written let a reader correctly refuse a cheap used Stoll as the FOUNDING buy while still treating it as a situational diligence-gated buy?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[4] (buy-used) and [0] (programmer dominates iron); glossary 'CAD/flat-knit programmer bottleneck' ('a Shima program is not a Stoll program'), 'Stoll flat-knit exit (2025)'; escalation_triggers[5] (ex-Stoll parts defer); round1_judgment Q6 (unresolved propose)
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap / unsynthesised tension: two correct pieces (buy-used-is-cheaper vs programmer-hinge-must-stay-on-a-live-toolchain) exist in separate parts of the spec but no single dominance rule adjudicates the used-Stoll case, so the specialist can be led into recommending a cheap dead-ecosystem machine for its most-strategic (programmer-anchoring) buy.
questions.why_load_bearing: the programmer is declared THE binding constraint ('program over metal'); anchoring it to a discontinued vendor for a founding machine directly undermines the strategy's own hinge, and this is exactly the surviving round-1 propose item that must converge or be flagged NOT-CONVERGED.

questions.q: Round 1 flagged (Q7, left as 'propose') that your 'periphery-only reverse-engineering rule' is a slogan plus two lists (core = needle bed/needles/cams/electronic selection/firmware/knit-CAD = NEVER; periphery = jigs/fixtures/gauges/spares = OK) with no test for the borderline parts a real builder faces. Give the OPERATIONAL decision test and apply it to three genuinely ambiguous parts — a needle-bed alignment gauge, a cam follower, and a yarn-path-touching carrier bracket — without letting the 'it's just a cheap spare' rationalisation erode the build-NEVER discipline into core-chain cloning by increments.
questions.targets: glossary 'periphery-only reverse-engineering rule' + 'core kinematic chain'; conflicts_and_dominance[6]; boundaries[2]; capabilities[4].method; round1_judgment Q7 (unresolved propose)
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap / non-operational rule in an OWNED deliverable: the reverse-engineering rule cannot adjudicate mechanically-adjacent borderline parts, which is precisely where the highest-confidence-NEVER discipline erodes in practice ('it's just a bracket'), so the specialist owns a rule it cannot actually run.
questions.why_load_bearing: the periphery-vs-core boundary is what keeps the build-NEVER verdict from being nibbled to death; a rule that cannot classify the ambiguous parts a maintainer/tinkerer actually encounters lets money-destroying, IP-exposing core-chain work in under a 'periphery spare' label — the second surviving round-1 propose item that must converge.

questions.q: Your whole-garment glossary prices used whole-garment machines at ~$20,000-90,000 [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED], yet your build-NEVER verdict rests on a headline 'sub-$20k used machine vs ~$2M-10M+ to build' order-of-magnitude comparison. A used whole-garment machine at $20k-90k is NOT sub-$20k. Does the whole-garment used band contradict or weaken the 'sub-$20k used' anchor, and does the build-NEVER order-of-magnitude argument still hold cleanly when the cheapest seamless option is 1-5x above the very anchor you quote against the $2M-10M+ build cost?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[1] (build NEVER, ~$2M-10M+ vs sub-$20k used); glossary 'whole-garment acquisition' (~$20k-90k used) and 'whole-garment no-linking trade'; capabilities[5].method; conflicts_and_dominance[7]
questions.failure_mode_probed: contradiction / internal figure inconsistency: the 'sub-$20k used' anchor that the build-NEVER order-of-magnitude claim leans on is contradicted by the specialist's own $20k-90k used whole-garment band, so the marquee comparison uses a best-case cheap-panel-machine anchor while a seamless machine costs several times that.
questions.why_load_bearing: build-NEVER is the highest-confidence verdict and its persuasiveness is the order-of-magnitude gap; if the specialist's own cheapest-seamless number breaches the 'sub-$20k' anchor, the comparison must be re-stated as 'orders of magnitude regardless of class' or it reads as cherry-picked, weakening the flagship conclusion.

questions.q: The linker is your named daily-output bottleneck and glossary 'linker bottleneck' concedes it is 'the role T1 names hardest to re-hire after the lean season.' Yet both your postures assume linker capacity is available: Phase-0 subcontract leans on the mesh's linkers and Phase-1 own-a-line requires you to hire and RETAIN them. Where in your capacity plan or acquisition ladder do you actually secure linker LABOUR SUPPLY (not just count linker seats), and is your 'buy-machine-plus-linkers-plus-programmer' framing quietly assuming a scarce, hard-to-re-hire, hand-skilled labour pool is simply purchasable on demand?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[0] (linker+programmer dominate; buy-without-linker = dead iron); glossary 'linker bottleneck' (hardest to re-hire); capabilities[1] (size off linker ceiling); decision_procedure step 3; validation_checklist (buy = buy-machine-plus-linkers-plus-programmer)
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap / hidden supply assumption: the specialist sizes capacity off the linker CEILING and warns a machine without a linker is dead iron, but never treats the SUPPLY of hard-to-re-hire hand-skilled linkers as its own constraint, so both the subcontract and own-a-line postures silently assume linker labour is available on demand.
questions.why_load_bearing: if linkers cannot be re-hired/retained in the lean season, the daily-output ceiling the whole line is sized against is itself unstable, and an owned line that clears the cost breakeven can still fail to ship because it cannot staff the binding step — a capacity risk the specialist owns but does not surface.

questions.q: You name design->knit-program assist as 'the highest-value AI use because it OFFSETS the scarce programmer,' while also declaring the programmer THE binding constraint and holding design->program AUTONOMY [UNKNOWN]. If AI only ASSISTS (human-in-the-loop, autonomy unproven), by how much does it actually relieve the binding constraint — and are you at risk of leaning your capacity/acquisition story on an AI programmer-offset whose magnitude is unmeasured, so the 'programmer bottleneck is winnable via AI' claim quietly does work that only proven autonomy could justify?
questions.targets: capabilities[5].method ('highest-value use... offsets the scarce programmer'); boundaries[3] (multiplier, autonomy [UNKNOWN]); escalation_triggers[4] (autonomy -> human_review); glossary 'CAD/flat-knit programmer bottleneck' ('winnable'), 'AI real-vs-hype boundary'; round1_judgment Q5 (watch)
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim / circular relief: the programmer is simultaneously 'the scarcest binding constraint' and 'the thing AI most offsets,' but with autonomy [UNKNOWN] and no measured uplift the offset magnitude is unknown, so calling the bottleneck 'winnable' via AI-assist risks smuggling in relief that only proven (currently [UNKNOWN]) autonomy would deliver.
questions.why_load_bearing: if the AI programmer-offset is quietly load-bearing in why the programmer bottleneck is 'winnable' and why an AI-design brand's strategy hinges here, an unmeasured assist magnitude means the hinge of the whole strategy rests on an [UNKNOWN]-autonomy claim wearing a 'multiplier' label — the exact N4 failure the loop guards.

questions.q: Whole-garment deletes your linker bottleneck entirely, and the linker is the constraint you say caps daily output — yet you hold whole-garment micro-economics [UNKNOWN] and file it as a 'later volume trade study, never a launch buy.' Is that [UNKNOWN] a genuine data gap or a convenient escape hatch that lets you avoid pricing the ONE option that dissolves your headline bottleneck? State the conditions under which whole-garment's deleted-linking value would actually beat the panel+linker path, or concede you cannot compare them and say why that is a real (not merely deferred) gap.
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[7] (whole-garment later trade study, micro-economics [UNKNOWN]); glossary 'whole-garment no-linking trade' + 'whole-garment acquisition'; capabilities[0]; kb2 WHOLEGARMENT_ACQUISITION
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap / escape-hatch [UNKNOWN]: the specialist declares the linker THE bottleneck yet parks the one machine class that deletes it under an [UNKNOWN] 'later trade study,' so the [UNKNOWN] may be shielding an uncomfortable comparison rather than flagging a real, conditioned data gap.
questions.why_load_bearing: if deleting the linker (the named daily-output ceiling) is worth pricing, dismissing whole-garment as [UNKNOWN]-and-later without stating the conditions that would flip it means the specialist never actually confronts whether its own bottleneck framing is escapable, leaving the capacity story one-sided.

questions.q: Round 1 proposed apply_now relabels for Q3 (throughput bands don't PROVE a 1:1 linker bottleneck), Q10 (capacity 'plan with counts' only producible as a structure-only sketch) and Q1 (undecomposed $2M-10M+). After those relabels, restate the linker-bottleneck claim, the capacity deliverable, and the build-cost magnitude in their corrected form: do the relabels actually FIX the overclaims (bands show balance-at-1:1 with linking hard-to-SCALE; a structure-only sketch not integer counts; an order-of-magnitude prior not a costed estimate), or do they merely soften wording while the spec elsewhere still promises 'the bands prove it,' 'the matching linker/programmer count named,' and a HIGH-confidence dollar figure?
questions.targets: capabilities[1].method + competency_questions_covered item 2 ('how do the throughput bands PROVE it'); capabilities[1].outputs + validation_checklist ('matching linker/programmer count named'); conflicts_and_dominance[1] + capabilities[5].method ($2M-10M+); round1_judgment Q1/Q3/Q10 (apply_now)
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim residue / cosmetic-fix risk: the round-1 apply_now edits may soften only one location while sibling text (competency_questions_covered, validation_checklist, other capability outputs) still asserts the un-corrected version, leaving the overclaim alive at a different spec address.
questions.why_load_bearing: the loop's verification re-greps for residue; if a corrected claim survives verbatim elsewhere in the spec, the fix is illusory and the specialist still over-promises (proof of a 1:1 bottleneck, named integer counts, a costed build figure) at a location the round-1 fix did not touch.

questions.failure_mode_probed: stale / post-cutoff drift: the machine-import cost stack and the market-structure read are anchored to 2025 facts and [UNKNOWN] 2025-26 changes, but from a mid-2026 vantage the specialist may present the 2025 duty stack and 'used pool has deepened' inferences as current rather than as needing a pre-buy refresh.

questions.q: Pull your whole acquisition verdict together against your hardest constraints: your first owned buy (Cixing-class used) may not hit your 12GG product gauge (Q1), a used-Stoll bargain endangers your programmer hinge (Q2), the linker labour you size against is hard to re-hire (Q5), the AI offset that makes the programmer 'winnable' is [UNKNOWN] in magnitude (Q6), your cheapest seamless option breaches your sub-$20k build-NEVER anchor (Q4), and the landed quote is still missing (Q9). Does your headline 'subcontract->buy-used->never-build' verdict survive all of these at once, or does honest aggregation force it to something weaker — e.g. 'subcontract indefinitely and do not own a line until a fine-gauge landed quote + a re-hirable linker pool + a live-toolchain machine + a measured programmer-offset all land'?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance (whole set); decision_procedure steps 4-7; capabilities[5] (merged verdict); validation_checklist (verdict names dominant constraint + review triggers); router standing_verdict (GATED); DECISION_MEMO gate G2
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim / verdict-over-aggregation: each caveat is individually acknowledged, but the merged 'subcontract->buy-used->never-build' verdict may present buy-used as a near-term reachable step when the honest conjunction of gates (gauge fit + linker supply + toolchain continuity + measured AI offset + landed quote + G2 rate) pushes the buy-used step much further out than the ladder implies.
questions.why_load_bearing: the merged verdict is the specialist's top-line owned deliverable; if it advertises buy-used as a normal next phase while the honest conjunction of its own unresolved gates keeps ownership out of reach, the specialist over-states how soon the brand can (or should) own iron, mis-guiding the capex decision the DECISION_MEMO's GATED posture depends on.
